clue.text: Sanctimonious author in hotel upset about heating, primarily

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the remaining piece
to upset something is to knock it over, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written, are the fodder

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: first letter of heating

explanation.surface: A smug writer staying at a hotel is upset about the heating arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does double duty in feel: the jumbled thirteen letters sit on either side of the single letter from heating, which lands in the middle of THAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-righteous who parades their moral superiority is described with this hyphenated adjective, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Interstellar object shall yet come around

indicators.note: to come around is to turn about, so the letters turn into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavenly body that promises it will return one day, as this one famously does every 76 years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come around' reads as the comet's periodic return, which is exactly why the surface is so apt; 'come' is both fodder and part of the indicator reading.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous periodic comet is a named celestial body travelling through space, though strictly it stays within our solar system.

clue.text: Musicians longing to hold note steadily at the start

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a longing is a lust
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of steadily

explanation.surface: Musicians yearning to sustain a note steadily right from its beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The note is from the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi, fa, so, la, ti); the container makes a single lute player and the final letter makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutists are players of the lute, so they are one particular kind of instrumental performer.

clue.text: Trainee initially ignored something profitable

indicators.note: ignoring what comes first means dropping the word's opening letter

parts.note: a trainee is a learner

explanation.surface: A trainee was overlooked at first but turned out to be a moneymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the L from LEARNER leaves the answer; L is also the learner-driver plate letter, which makes the removal feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner, as in 'a nice little earner', is informal British for a venture or asset that brings in money.

clue.text: Many people run in beachwear

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy swimsuit or, in Australia, a flip-flop
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Crowds of people go running in their swimwear, perhaps at a beach charity race.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside THONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd, a dense mass of people gathered together in one place.

clue.text: Makes do, learning from old grannie?

definitions.text: Makes do, learning from old grannie?

parts.words: Makes do, learning from old grannie
parts.note: surface reading: getting by with little, picking up wisdom from an elderly grandmother

parts.words: Makes do, learning from old grannie
parts.note: setter's reading: rearranging the letters of 'old' produces 'do', and those of 'grannie' produce 'earning', within 'learning'

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes by frugally, having picked up the knack from a thrifty old grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'makes' as a verb acting on words: shuffling OLD gives DO and shuffling GRANNIE gives EARNING. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb here means rearranges letters into new words, which is exactly what turning OLD into DO involves.

clue.text: Consultant ultimately subject to regular review for being controversial online

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: last letter of consultant
a rolling review is one repeated at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A consultant whose work is constantly under review is accused of stirring up trouble on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' describes contracts or reviews renewed continuously, as in a rolling programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Posting deliberately provocative or inflammatory messages on the internet to provoke a reaction is called by this name.

clue.text: Exceeded the limit in a Rover, travelling north

indicators.note: things travelling are moving about, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone got a speeding ticket driving their Rover car up the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling north' in a down clue tempts a reversal, but nothing reversed fits; 'north' is just N and 'travelling' shuffles it with A ROVER. Rover is a British car make.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go beyond an intended boundary, time or amount, so the past tense matches going past a limit.

clue.text: King and others returned in due course

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
et al. is the Latin abbreviation meaning and others

explanation.surface: The monarch and his entourage came home eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of R plus ET AL is turned round, not just the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at some future time, eventually rather than now, so they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Clear initial couple of requirements when working with editor

indicators.note: an initial couple is the first two, so only the opening pair of letters is kept

parts.note: keeping only the opening two letters of the word, as the selector asks
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a machine that is on is working
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A job spec that clearly sets out the first requirements for working alongside an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like a verb or part of the wordplay but is the adjective definition; the four short pieces simply join up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned argument is logical and well thought out, which makes it clear and coherent.

clue.text: French lady produced wine around Italy

parts.note: to produce is to make

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Moselle is a German white wine
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman makes wine in the region around Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Moselle is a river running through France and Germany, whose valley gives its name to the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for an unmarried woman, the equivalent of Miss in English.

clue.text: Each increasingly uncompromising person from New York, say

parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each
more stern, the comparative of stern

explanation.surface: A New Yorker who gets tougher and more unbending by the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increasingly' signals a comparative adjective, so 'uncompromising' becomes STERNER rather than STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: New York lies on the east coast of the US, so its residents are an example of people from the East.

clue.text: Grub is hot stuff, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so it is judged by sound not spelling

parts.note: lava is molten rock, literally hot stuff

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a dish as spicy and delicious, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like slang for food, which makes 'hot stuff' feel like chilli; in a non-rhotic British accent the R is silent, so the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft wormlike young of an insect, the stage biologists call by this name.

clue.text: Very, very meh!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two words each meaning very, as in 'so good'
second meaning: mediocre, neither good nor bad

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated intensifier sits oddly next to the shrug of 'meh'; read it as two small words stuck together rather than an emphatic phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubling the intensifier literally spells the phrase, while as an adjective it means middling or unremarkable, just like the slang shrug.

clue.text: Celebrity artist with some money, but no power

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: saying 'but no' excludes something, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: pence are British coins, a small sum of money
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A famous artist who has some cash yet holds no real influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is known for her unmade bed exhibit; removing the P from PENCE leaves ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is fame or high standing, so it works as a noun for the state of being well known and distinguished.

clue.text: Item of interest in piece of info presented by a broadcaster in Ireland

parts.note: taken as written
RTÉ is Ireland's national broadcaster
a fact is one piece of information

explanation.surface: An Irish TV channel presents an interesting snippet of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but only links definition to wordplay; 'presented by' means the broadcaster's part comes first. RTÉ is Ireland's public service broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a man-made object of historical or cultural significance, such as an item in a museum.

clue.text: A melon is dished out for pudding, perhaps

indicators.note: food dished out is spread across plates, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Melon is served up as a dessert course.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' shows the definition is by example: this is one kind of pudding, not a synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina, coarse wheat grains cooked in sweet milk, is a classic British school dessert, so an example of a pudding.

clue.text: Network computer attached to old, second-rate monitor

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
B grade is second class, below A
a server is the computer that runs a network

explanation.surface: A network machine is hooked up to an ancient, poor-quality screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' wants to be a computer screen, fitting the surface; it is the definition as a person who watches.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor, such as an election monitor, is someone who watches and reports on proceedings, just like an observer.

clue.text: Unpleasant individual, 13?
Food cooked principally in Chinese way?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Tao is the Way in Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of cooked

explanation.surface: Is this food prepared mainly in the Chinese style?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the irony: the answer is Mexican, not Chinese at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with a savoury filling, so it is a kind of dish one eats.

clue.text: The sound of a radio transmitter is picked up

indicators.note: the sound of something is how it is heard, so it is judged by pronunciation

parts.note: a radio mast carries the transmitting aerial

explanation.surface: The noise from a radio transmitter is detected by a receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' in a radio context means received, which suits the surface; here it means gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate, so the past participle matches collecting things up.

clue.text: Go and remain occupied in some activity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang command to leave, clear off
second meaning: read as three words, to be busy doing something

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the letters differently: BE AT IT, as in 'they're still at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang imperative orders someone away, while the split phrase describes keeping busy with an ongoing task.

clue.text: Constant warning light for curvy section of road

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
amber is the traffic light warning before red

explanation.surface: A permanent warning light is put up for a bendy stretch of road.
explanation.walkthrough: Traffic lights fit the road picture neatly; the constant is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight convex curve across a road surface that lets rainwater drain off to the sides.

clue.text: Avoid publicity during the period before an event

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the eve is the day or time just before an occasion
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A celebrity keeps out of the limelight in the run-up to a big occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid publicity' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or dodge something, which is a straightforward synonym for keeping away from it.

clue.text: Items that collapse in messy heap, sorta

indicators.note: messy means disordered, so the letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Things fall down into an untidy pile, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The slangy 'sorta' is there for its letters, not its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat with a spring mechanism, so it can be folded flat and stored under a theatre seat.

clue.text: Visionary concept catalogue

parts.note: a concept is an idea
a catalogue is a list

explanation.walkthrough: Three words, three roles: definition first, then two synonyms joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is a dreamer who pursues lofty ideals, so the noun is a close synonym for such a person.

clue.text: Wooden crosspiece protecting small plant

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it all round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a bail is one of the small wooden pieces resting on top of cricket stumps
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A wooden frame is set up to shelter a little seedling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bails sit across the tops of the three stumps; S goes inside BAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb grown for cooking, so it is one example of a plant.

clue.text: Tricky game?

parts.note: surface reading: a game that is hard to master
setter's reading: a card game played in tricks, where the bidding side must win a set number of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' means difficult on the surface, but here it means consisting of tricks, the rounds of cards won in play.
explanation.definitionFit: This partnership card game is scored by winning tricks, and it is famously demanding, so both senses of tricky apply.
